rules.rule: Check for HIV PEP: exposure to infectious fluid or human bite
rules.problem: Trigger is broader than the page (any body fluid, any human bite) and check_for lists a bare Bleeding finding; also omits blood-stained fluid/tissue and the follow-up qualifier (sexual contact, sharps injury, splash to eye/open wound/mouth/nose). Page header is a management-style question, so a check task is reasonable.

rules.rule: Urgent: HIV PEP, exposure to infectious fluid or bleeding human bite
rules.problem: Structure (or of fluids, and of bite+bleeding) matches the red box; Urgent justified by 'Give urgent attention'. Minor: the box says a bleeding bite needs hepatitis B prevention only, no HIV PEP, so Urgent is for exposure work-up not HIV PEP specifically; blood-stained fluid/tissue not encoded.

summary: The priority rule faithfully reflects the red box entry conditions. The check task's trigger is broader than the page: generic Body fluid exposure includes non-infectious fluids, any human bite fires it though only bleeding bites count, and Bleeding stands alone in check_for. No invented clinical content; all SNOMED concepts exist.
